question: A 12 V source is connected across R1 = 2 kOhm and R2 = 4 kOhm in series. Find the voltage across R2.
A 9 V battery feeds three resistors in series: 1 kOhm, 2 kOhm and 6 kOhm. Find the current in the circuit.
A 24 V supply drives R1 = 4 kOhm in series with the parallel combination of R2 = 12 kOhm and R3 = 6 kOhm. Find the voltage across R3.
A 10 V source drives a 100 Ohm resistor in series with two 200 Ohm resistors in parallel. Find the total current drawn from the source.
A 5 mA DC current source feeds a 2 kOhm resistor in parallel with a 3 kOhm resistor. Find the voltage across the resistors.
A 20 V source is connected in series with R1 = 1 kOhm and R2 = 3 kOhm. Find the power dissipated in R2.
A 15 V source supplies R1 = 5 kOhm in series with R2 = 10 kOhm. Find the power delivered by the source.
work: I = 1 mA; P = 15 V * 1 mA = 15 mW

question: A 10 V source in series with R1 = 2 kOhm connects to node a, and a 5 V source in series with R2 = 2 kOhm also connects to node a. Both sources have their negative terminals at ground and positive terminals toward the resistors. A 1 kOhm resistor R3 connects node a to ground. Find the voltage at node a.

A Wheatstone bridge is fed by a 10 V source connected between node t and ground. Branch 1: R1 = 1 kOhm from t to node a and R2 = 2 kOhm from a to ground. Branch 2: R3 = 2 kOhm from t to node b and R4 = 1 kOhm from b to ground. Find the voltage V(a,b) between nodes a and b.

A Wheatstone bridge is fed by a 10 V source connected between node t and ground. R1 = 1 kOhm from t to node a, R2 = 2 kOhm from a to ground, R3 = 2 kOhm from t to node b, R4 = 1 kOhm from b to ground, and R5 = 1 kOhm connects a to b. Find the current through R5.
A 10 V source in series with R1 = 5 kOhm feeds node x. A 2 mA current source pushes current from ground into node x. R2 = 5 kOhm connects x to ground. Find the voltage at node x.
Find the Thevenin equivalent at terminals a-b: a 30 V source in series with 6 kOhm connects to terminal a, a 3 kOhm resistor connects a to b, and b is the negative terminal of the source.

A 12 V source in series with 4 kOhm connects to terminal a, and a 4 kOhm resistor connects a to terminal b, which is the negative terminal of the source. Find the Norton current and Norton resistance at a-b.
Find the equivalent resistance between terminals a and b: R1 = 2 kOhm from a to node c, R2 = 6 kOhm from c to b, and R3 = 3 kOhm from c to b.

A 24 V source in series with 2 kOhm connects to node a, a 6 kOhm resistor connects a to ground, and a 1.5 kOhm resistor connects a to terminal b. Find the Thevenin voltage and resistance between b and ground.

A 4 mA current source pushes current from ground into node x. A 2 kOhm resistor connects x to ground, and a 1 kOhm resistor connects x to terminal a. Find the Thevenin voltage and resistance between a and ground.

A 10 V source in series with R1 = 1 kOhm feeds node x, and R2 = 1 kOhm connects x to ground. A voltage-controlled voltage source with gain 5, controlled by the voltage at x, drives node out (negative terminal at ground). A 2 kOhm load connects out to ground. Find Vout.

A 2 V source sets the voltage at node a (negative terminal at ground), and a 1 kOhm resistor R1 connects a to ground. A voltage-controlled current source with transconductance 3 mS pushes a current of 3 mS times Va from ground into node b. R2 = 1 kOhm connects b to ground. Find the voltage at node b.
work: I = 3m*2 = 6 mA into b; Vb = 6 V

question: A 5 V source in series with a 1 kOhm resistor forms a loop with current Ix. A current-controlled current source pushes 10 times Ix into node y, and a 500 Ohm resistor connects y to ground. Find the voltage at node y.
work: Ix = 5 mA; 50 mA * 500 = 25 V (sign depends on direction)

question: A 6 V source in series with a 2 kOhm resistor forms a loop with current I. A current-controlled voltage source with transresistance 500 Ohm produces a voltage of 500 times I at node z (negative terminal at ground), and a 1 kOhm resistor connects z to ground. Find the voltage at node z.
work: I = 3 mA; 500*3m = 1.5 V (sign depends on direction)

question: A 1 mA current source pushes current from ground into node x, R1 = 1 kOhm connects x to ground, and a voltage-controlled current source draws 0.5 mS times Vx out of node x to ground. Find the voltage at node x.
An RC low-pass filter with R = 1 kOhm and C = 0.1 uF is driven by a 1 V amplitude AC source at 1 kHz. Find the magnitude of the output voltage across the capacitor.
A 10 V amplitude AC source at 1 kHz drives R = 100 Ohm in series with L = 10 mH. Find the magnitude of the current.
A series RC circuit with R = 1 kOhm and C = 1 uF is driven by a 5 V amplitude AC source at 100 Hz. Find the magnitude of the voltage across the resistor.
Find the magnitude of the impedance of a 100 Ohm resistor in series with a 1 uF capacitor at 1 kHz.
An RC low-pass filter has R = 10 kOhm and C = 10 nF. Find the cutoff frequency.
An RC high-pass filter has C = 0.47 uF in series with the input and R = 1 kOhm from the output to ground. Find the cutoff frequency.
An RL low-pass filter has L = 100 mH in series with the input and R = 1 kOhm from the output to ground. Find the cutoff frequency.
An RC low-pass filter has R1 = 1 kOhm in series and C = 1 uF from the output to ground, and a load RL = 1 kOhm is connected across C. Find the DC gain and the cutoff frequency.
Two identical RC low-pass sections are cascaded without a buffer: R1 = 1 kOhm, C1 = 1 uF, then R2 = 1 kOhm, C2 = 1 uF, with the output across C2. Find the -3 dB cutoff frequency.
Find the pole of the transfer function of an RC low-pass filter with R = 2 kOhm and C = 5 uF.
A series RLC circuit has R = 20 Ohm, L = 50 mH and C = 2 uF, driven by an AC source with the output across R. Find the resonant frequency.
A series RLC circuit with R = 5 Ohm, L = 1 mH and C = 100 nF is driven by an AC source, with the output taken across R. Find the quality factor and the bandwidth.
A parallel RLC tank with R = 10 kOhm, L = 10 mH and C = 100 nF, all connected between node a and ground, is driven by a 1 mA AC current source into node a. Find the resonant frequency.
A series RLC circuit with R = 10 Ohm, L = 1 mH and C = 1 uF is driven by a 10 V amplitude AC source at 5.033 kHz. Find the magnitude of the current.
work: 5.033 kHz is resonance (5032.9 Hz): X ~ 0, |Z| = 10 Ohm, I = 1 A

question: A resistor R = 4.7 kOhm in series with a capacitor C = 10 uF is charged from a 5 V step source. Find the time constant.
A 10 V DC source drives an RL circuit with L = 50 mH and R = 250 Ohm in series. Find the time constant.
A capacitor C = 2 uF is charged from a 12 V source through R1 = 3 kOhm, and R2 = 6 kOhm is connected in parallel with the capacitor. Find the time constant.
An inductor L = 10 mH is fed from a 5 V source through R1 = 100 Ohm, and R2 = 100 Ohm is connected in parallel with the inductor. Find the time constant.
Find the output voltage of a voltage divider made of R1 and R2 fed by a source Vs, with the output taken across R2.
